headline: Ensure Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and related distribution infrastructure, preventing these expenses from being shifted to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor's administration, Dominion Energy (with amendments)
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users
news_headline: Virginia orders data centers to pay for grid upgrades in new policy draft
news_summary: Virginia regulators are shifting more of the costs for new power infrastructure, driven by data center buildout, directly to the facilities creating the demand. This policy aims to reduce the financial burden on households and small businesses for grid upgrades tied to the state's largest new electricity users.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers monthly, enhancing transparency regarding their water usage and environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making these figures publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This initiative aims to provide transparency and better inform discussions about the environmental footprint of the rapidly growing data center industry.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high-energy use data centers, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to demand impact evaluations on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: Virginia's new budget regulates data center noise levels
news_summary: Virginia's new budget includes legislation like HB 153, which imposes stricter siting and permitting requirements for large-scale data centers. These new rules mandate sound assessments for residences and schools within a 500-foot radius and allow localities to require impact evaluations on various environmental and community aspects.
